questions.q: Who is the architect of the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world as of 2022?
questions.n: Adrian Smith was the design partner at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) responsible for the buttressed core design of the Burj Khalifa.

questions.q: What was the tallest skyscraper in the world in 1930?
o: The Woolworth Building (often cited for its 1913-1930 reign) or the Chrysler Building (completed in 1930).
40 Wall Street (The Bank of Manhattan Building)
questions.n: The Woolworth Building held the title until 1930, when the Chrysler Building surpassed it shortly before the Empire State was finished.

questions.q: Who designed the Petronas Twin Towers in Malaysia?
questions.n: Pelli designed the towers with an eight-pointed star plan based on Islamic geometric patterns.

questions.q: What is the "first project" or major work of Leandro Locsin, originally his thesis?
o: The Chapel of the Holy Sacrifice (UP Diliman).
The Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP)
questions.n: This circular chapel with a thin-shell concrete dome was Locsin's first major breakthrough.

questions.q: Which structure is considered the first earthquake-resistant building in the Philippines?
o: The Main Building of the University of Santo Tomas (UST).
questions.n: Designed by Fr. Roque Ruaño, it features a unique system of separate concrete modules to withstand seismic activity.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the TWA Flight Center (TWA Airport)?
questions.n: His expressionistic design uses thin-shell concrete to mimic the look of a bird in flight.

questions.q: Identify the architect of the Robie House.
questions.n: The Robie House is considered the greatest example of his Prairie School style.

questions.q: Who designed the National Museum of Western Art in Tokyo, Japan?
questions.n: This is Le Corbusier's only building in the Far East, completed with the help of his Japanese apprentices.

questions.q: Which Catalan architect is known for the "Trencadis" (mosaic) technique and the Sagrada Familia?
questions.n: Gaudi's organic architecture is defined by the use of broken tile mosaics and his unfinished cathedral.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the Marquette Building in Chicago?
questions.n: This firm was a pillar of the Chicago School and completed the Marquette Building in 1895.

questions.q: Who designed the Philam Life Building in United Nations Avenue, Manila?
questions.n: He designed this International Style landmark, which was recently part of a major redevelopment controversy.

questions.q: The "sail-like" structure of the 20th century refers to which building?
questions.n: Utzon's design for the shells is universally compared to the sails of a ship.

questions.q: Identify the architect of the Old Iloilo City Hall (Art Deco design).
questions.n: Arellano was the master of Art Deco in the Philippines, also designing the Metropolitan Theater.

questions.q: Who designed the Olympic Stadium in Mexico (1951-52)?
questions.n: He was the lead architect, working alongside Raúl Salinas and Jorge Bravo.

questions.q: Which architectural style is the Hagia Sophia classified under?
questions.n: Hagia Sophia is the quintessential Byzantine work, featuring the use of pendentives to support a massive dome.

questions.q: What are the three Greek Orders of Architecture?
questions.n: These represent the chronological and stylistic evolution of classical Greek column design.

questions.q: What are the two Roman Orders of Architecture (additions to the Greek)?
questions.n: The Romans simplified the Doric to create the Tuscan and combined Ionic and Corinthian to create the Composite.

questions.q: Which prehistoric burial consists of a mound with a long narrow path leading to a gallery?
questions.n: A passage grave is characterized by a distinct narrow passage leading to a central burial chamber.

questions.q: Which burial place faces North and South with a long narrow path leading to an open court?
questions.n: The court tomb is defined by an uncovered area at the entrance where rituals were likely held.

questions.q: Define a "Wedge Tomb" in prehistoric architecture.
o: A burial chamber that tapers in both height and width at one end.
A tomb built into the side of a cliff.
A tomb shaped like a circular wheel.
A tomb that is used specifically for children.
questions.n: This tapering 'wedge' shape gives the tomb its name.

questions.q: A Paleolithic structure house that is inclined on one side of a cave is called?
questions.n: A lean-to is a simple shelter supported on one side, often against a cave wall or trees.

questions.q: What is a Paleolithic "Hut" typically made of?
questions.n: Paleolithic humans used readily available organic materials from their environment.

questions.q: "As an architect, you design for the present, with an awareness of the past, for a future which is essentially unknown." Whose dictum is this?
questions.n: This reflects Foster's philosophy of high-tech architecture that respects historical context.

questions.q: "The purpose of architecture is to shelter and enhance man's life on earth and to fulfill his belief in the nobility of his existence." Whose dictum is this?
questions.n: Saarinen's work often sought to express spiritual or noble aspiration through form.

questions.q: "Form follows function" is the famous dictum of?
questions.n: Sullivan believed that the shape of a building should be primarily based on its intended function.

questions.q: Which civilization contributed the vertical scroll (volute) found in the Ionic order?
o: The Greeks (though influenced by West Asiatic/Persian motifs).
questions.n: The Ionic order originated in Ionia (western Turkey) and was adopted as a primary Greek order.

questions.q: What is a characteristic of Persian Architecture columns?
o: Use of double-bull or double-unicorn capital (protomes).
questions.n: Persian columns at Persepolis are famous for these distinctive animal-shaped capitals.

questions.q: What is the primary material used in Greek Architecture?
questions.n: The abundance of high-quality marble allowed Greeks to achieve high precision in their monuments.

questions.q: Which civilization used massive openings and developed the true arch?
questions.n: The development of the arch, vault, and dome allowed Romans to span vast interior spaces.

questions.q: What is the orientation of a typical rectangular Greek temple?
questions.n: Greeks usually oriented temples so the rising sun would illuminate the cult statue through the entrance.

questions.q: The "Greatest Civilizations" were often found in which climate?
questions.n: Fertile soil and water management in these areas supported the first dense urban centers.

questions.q: What is the climate of Greece that affected its open-air social activities?
o: Mediterranean climate (hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters).
questions.n: The bright sun and clear air encouraged the outdoor life seen in theaters and agoras.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao?
questions.n: This titanium-clad masterpiece is a landmark of Deconstructivism.

questions.q: Which architect is associated with the "Bahay Kubo" inspired Coconut Palace?
questions.n: Mañosa dedicated his career to developing a distinct Filipino architectural identity.

questions.q: What was the tallest building in 1931?
o: Empire State Building (Ar. Shreve, Lamb & Harmon).
questions.n: It held the title of the world's tallest building for 40 years until 1971.

questions.q: In Theory of Architecture, what refers to the relative size of a structure to a human?
questions.n: Scale is the perception of size relative to a standard, usually the human body ('human scale').

questions.q: What refers to the pleasing relationship between parts of a whole?
questions.n: Proportion involves the ratios between different dimensions of a design.

questions.q: Identify the architect of the Villa Farnese.
questions.n: Vignola was a leading architect of the Mannerist period and designer of this pentagonal villa.

questions.q: What is the "Piazza Farnese" known for?
o: A busy commercial market in modern Italy.
Being a major High Renaissance square in Rome.
The site of the first gladiator matches.
A famous garden designed by Capability Brown.
questions.n: It is framed by the Palazzo Farnese and features two granite basins from the Baths of Caracalla.

questions.q: Which cathedral is a masterpiece of French Gothic architecture?
questions.n: Known for its stunning stained glass and flying buttresses, it is the model for High Gothic.

questions.q: When was RA 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) signed/approved?
questions.n: This is the official date of signing for the current law governing the architecture profession in the Philippines.

questions.q: A newly passed architect shall be ____ to become a member of the IAPOA.
o: Required to take an entrance exam
questions.n: Under RA 9266, registration as an architect automatically includes membership in the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects.

questions.q: What is DAEDS?
o: Daily Architectural and Engineering Data Sheets
Detailed Architectural and Environmental Design Services
Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services.
Director of Architectural Engineering and Design Standards
questions.n: This refers to the comprehensive package of architectural and engineering plans.

questions.q: What is DADS?
questions.n: This refers to the architectural design services specifically, excluding the engineering components.

questions.q: Under SPP Doc 202, what percentage of the fee is paid upon completion of the Contract Document Phase?
questions.n: Completion of construction documents marks a major milestone, typically triggering a cumulative total of 90% (85% to 90%) depending on the specific breakdown of the 100% fee.

questions.q: What is the "Acceptance Fee" or signing of the agreement fee?
questions.n: This initial payment covers the mobilization and acceptance of the architectural commission.

questions.q: If construction is suspended for more than ____, the fee for the remaining works shall be doubled.
questions.n: A suspension of half a year justifies an increase in fees due to the effort of remobilization and potential cost changes.

questions.q: In the Method of Compensation, what is MDPE?
o: Management of Design and Personnel Effort
questions.n: This method multiplies the technical salaries by a factor to cover overhead and profit.

questions.q: What bond is required to guarantee the quality of materials and workmanship for a period of one year?
questions.n: The guarantee bond ensures that the contractor will fix defects appearing within a year after completion.

questions.q: What bond guarantees that the contractor will complete the project?
questions.n: The performance bond protects the owner if the contractor fails to finish the project according to plans.
